newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Independent Venezuelan oil operators lift output.
newsitem.headline: Independent Venezuelan oil operators lift output.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Lagoven said on Monday that production from its independently-operated fields rose by 130 percent in 1996 to an average of 62,000 barrels per day (bpd).

One crude stream which contributed to the rise was a new light crude from deep strata in the old Jusepin field. Another was the exploration well SLL-1X in the Quiriquire field which was producing at nearly 1,600 bpd of light crude and 11.9 million cubic feet of gas daily. Also, well TEX-59 in the Monagas Sur field was producing 5,000 bpd of crude, Lagoven said.

Independent producers working with Lagoven, a subsidiary of Venezuela's oil giant PDVSA, include Total; British Petroleum; a Maxus -Otepi-British Petroleum consortium ; a Benton -Vinccler consortium; and Shell.
